text: x is the modulus the docstring calls p, and y is the exponent it calls n
n is the second argument y and p is the first argument x
2 XOR n, which is what the operator ^ means in Python
any integer congruent to 2^n modulo p; for example candidate(0, 1) may return 1 instead of 0
for y = 0 the call must raise an exception, as division by zero does in Python
p denotes a prime (every example uses one of the primes 5, 11, 101), so calls with a non-prime y are outside the contract
any value numerically equal to the residue is acceptable, for example the float 3.0
the computation must be efficient for large n, for example by modular exponentiation rather than forming 2^n in full
